assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
subdomain scope is base model selection and matching for fine-tuned specialist LLMs in orchestrated systems
evaluation is task-metric-centric with quality floor as non-negotiable gate
orchestration of multiple specialists is the production context; single-model selection is a degenerate case
exclusions: full pretraining and continued pretraining execution (referenced only as domain uplift assessment)
data pipeline construction and annotation management
online A/B testing and experimentation framework
safety and alignment fine-tuning beyond quality floor definition

competency_questions.question: What task profile constraints gate which base models are eligible for each specialist?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TASK_PROFILE, LICENSE_TOS, QUALITY_FLOOR define eligibility gates

competency_questions.question: How is the minimum acceptable quality bar set and enforced in the model selection process?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QUALITY_FLOOR defines numeric threshold and EVAL_HARNESS enforces it

competency_questions.question: How is benchmark contamination detected and mitigated to prevent Goodhart gaming of model selection?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BENCHMARK_CONTAMINATION + GOODHART_GUARD define detection and mitigation protocol

competency_questions.question: How is the cost/quality/latency Pareto frontier mapped and which operating point is chosen?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COST_QUALITY_TRADEOFF produces Pareto chart; QUALITY_FLOOR and LATENCY_BUDGET define feasible region

competency_questions.question: When should a fine-tuned small specialist beat a large generalist and what evidence is required?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NARROW_TASK_SPECIALIST_WIN + GENERALIST_VS_SPECIALIST define criteria and evidence requirements

competency_questions.question: How is the decision between LoRA and full fine-tuning made given GPU budget and task requirements?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LORA_VS_FULL_FINETUNE defines decision criteria and SERVING_OVERHEAD_MODEL validates serving feasibility

competency_questions.question: What is the fallback policy when a specialist model fails and how are fallback costs bounded?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FALLBACK_POLICY defines chain and MULTI_SPECIALIST_COST models fallback cost impact

competency_questions.question: How is domain-specific pretraining assessed and when does it justify choosing a domain base model?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DOMAIN_SPECIFIC_PRETRAIN defines assessment and uplift quantification method

competency_questions.question: How is knowledge distillation policy constrained by teacher model licensing and ToS?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ORCA_DISTILL_POLICY + LICENSE_TOS define permissible distillation approaches

competency_questions.question: How are multi-specialist orchestration cost and latency modeled across the full specialist chain?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MULTI_SPECIALIST_COST models aggregate system; LATENCY_BUDGET validates chain

competency_questions.question: How is the model selection record made auditable and how are re-evaluation triggers defined?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SELECTION_RECORD and RE_EVAL_CADENCE define documentation and trigger protocol

competency_questions.question: How does quantization impact quality and serving cost, and how is the acceptable quantization level determined?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QUANTIZATION_IMPACT defines measurement; QUALITY_FLOOR and SERVING_OVERHEAD_MODEL define constraints

glossary.definition: minimum acceptable task metric score below which no model is deployable regardless of cost or latency advantage
set of model options where no alternative dominates on both cost and quality simultaneously
low-rank adaptation: parameter-efficient fine-tuning injecting small rank-decomposed weight matrices into frozen base model layers
overlap between a model's training data and the evaluation benchmark dataset, inflating apparent performance
a fine-tuned model optimized for a narrow, well-defined task domain within an orchestrated multi-model system
large frontier model capable of broad task coverage without task-specific fine-tuning, typically accessed via API
when a measure becomes a target it ceases to be a good measure; benchmark scores optimized by model vendors lose predictive validity for task quality
training a smaller student model on outputs from a larger teacher model to transfer capability without full pretraining cost
structured specification of a specialist's input/output format, quality requirements, latency SLA, throughput, and context length constraints

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for specialist-to-model matching work units in absence of supplied datasets; informed by Huyen Designing Machine Learning Systems model selection and cost chapters
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Huyen, Chip. Designing Machine Learning Systems. O'Reilly 2022. Chapters on model selection, cost, and evaluation.
grounding_limits: domain-general heuristic priors for LLM engineering

nodes.definition: Elicit and document the specialist's task profile: input/output format, context length, latency SLA, throughput needs, and quality bar before selecting any base model.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: task scope changes or new specialist added

pros.claim: Front-loads constraint discovery so model selection is grounded, not aspirational
pros.example: discovered 32k context need ruled out 4B-param model

cons.claim: Poorly specified profiles cause late-stage model re-selection churn
cons.example: SLA discovered post-training forced model swap

failure_modes: underspecifying latency/throughput budget
conflating nice-to-have with hard constraints
acceptance_tests: task profile doc approved by domain SME
all SLA numbers have measurement methodology
revisit_triggers: specialist task scope expands beyond original profile
new latency/throughput constraint imposed

nodes.definition: Audit candidate base models for training-data contamination of evaluation benchmarks used to measure task performance, flagging Goodhart-law risk where leaderboard scores overstate real-world utility.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new benchmark or model card released

pros.claim: Prevents selecting a model that memorized the eval set
pros.example: model aced MMLU but failed on held-out domain tasks

cons.claim: Full contamination audits are expensive and rarely complete
cons.example: card rarely discloses full training mixture

failure_modes: trusting vendor leaderboard scores without contamination check
using same benchmark for both selection and final eval
acceptance_tests: each benchmark scored for contamination risk
at least one uncontaminated eval included in selection protocol
revisit_triggers: new model released with undisclosed training data
eval benchmark recycled from prior model's training window

nodes.definition: Verify that each candidate base model's license and terms of service permit the intended deployment: commercial use, fine-tuning, distillation, output commercialization, and orchestration in multi-model pipelines.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: model license updated or business use case changes

pros.claim: Eliminates legally blocked models before GPU spend
pros.example: non-commercial-only model used in product causes takedown

cons.claim: License grey-areas for distillation and LoRA adapters require legal interpretation
cons.example: LoRA of CC-BY-NC model used commercially — contested

failure_modes: ignoring fine-tuning restriction clauses
using distillation-prohibited model as teacher
acceptance_tests: sign-off from legal team or counsel
compliance decision documented in model selection record
revisit_triggers: model license changes post-selection
business use case extends to new deployment region

nodes.definition: Map the Pareto frontier of model candidates across cost-per-token, quality (task metric), and P99 latency to identify which models dominate and where acceptable tradeoffs exist given budget constraints.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: inference pricing changes or new model released

pros.claim: Makes tradeoff explicit so stakeholders can choose informed operating points
pros.example: identified 7B model at 1/8 cost within 2% quality of 70B

cons.claim: Pareto frontier shifts with pricing and model releases; analysis has short shelf-life
cons.example: GPT-4o price cut invalidated prior tradeoff map

failure_modes: optimizing cost alone ignoring quality floor
omitting latency from tradeoff surface
acceptance_tests: Pareto chart includes at least 3 models
budget feasibility sign-off from finance
revisit_triggers: pricing change exceeds 20%
new model enters Pareto frontier
latency SLA tightened

nodes.definition: Empirically test whether a strong generalist base model (e.g. frontier API model) already meets task quality and latency targets before committing to specialist fine-tuning, establishing the performance gap that fine-tuning must close.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new frontier model released or task quality bar raised

pros.claim: Avoids expensive fine-tuning when frontier model prompt-engineering suffices
pros.example: GPT-4o with 5-shot beats fine-tuned 7B on clinical NER

cons.claim: Generalist API cost at scale may exceed fine-tuned local model cost
cons.example: GPT-4o at 10M tokens/day unaffordable vs self-hosted 7B

failure_modes: comparing generalist zero-shot against fine-tuned specialist unfairly
ignoring latency/cost when generalist quality is sufficient
acceptance_tests: generalist evaluation uses same eval set as specialist
decision gate: fine-tune only if gap > quality threshold or cost > budget
revisit_triggers: frontier model capability jump narrows gap
task quality threshold lowered by product

nodes.definition: Decide between parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA/QLoRA/adapters) and full fine-tuning based on task adaptation depth, GPU memory budget, catastrophic forgetting risk, and serving inference overhead.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: GPU memory budget changes or LoRA quality gap closes

pros.claim: LoRA reduces GPU memory 4-8x enabling larger base models on same hardware
pros.example: QLoRA trains 70B on 2x40GB vs 8x80GB for full FT

cons.claim: LoRA may not match full FT on tasks requiring deep weight redistribution
cons.example: code generation tasks show 3-5% quality gap for low-rank LoRA

failure_modes: choosing rank too low causing underfitting
ignoring adapter merging cost at inference for multiple specialists
acceptance_tests: rank selection justified by intrinsic dimensionality estimate
memory budget verified against training hardware
revisit_triggers: quality gap between LoRA and full FT exceeds threshold
serving latency overhead from adapter switching becomes bottleneck

nodes.definition: Produce a ranked shortlist of 3-5 base model candidates per specialist that pass license, cost, latency, and quality-gap filters, with rationale documented for each included and excluded candidate.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new model family released or major version update

pros.claim: Structured shortlist prevents ad-hoc model choices and ensures auditability
pros.example: shortlist doc required for model governance review

cons.claim: Shortlist staleness risk as model landscape evolves faster than review cycles
cons.example: shortlist from 6 months ago excludes Llama 3.x entirely

failure_modes: shortlisting only from one vendor family
excluding open-weight models without cost comparison
acceptance_tests: shortlist includes at least one open-weight and one API option if available
exclusion rationale documented for every rejected candidate
revisit_triggers: shortlisted model deprecated or weights removed
governance review flags missing candidate family

nodes.definition: Select the appropriate parameter scale (sub-1B, 1-7B, 7-13B, 13-70B, 70B+) for the specialist by balancing task complexity against inference cost, latency, and hardware constraints.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: task complexity changes or hardware tier changes

pros.claim: Right-sized model avoids over-provisioning GPU compute for simple tasks
pros.example: extraction NLP task solved by 7B at 1/20 cost of 70B

cons.claim: Scaling laws for fine-tuned specialist quality are domain-specific and uncertain
cons.example: law predictions off by 10% quality points on narrow domain

failure_modes: undersizing for reasoning-heavy tasks
ignoring KV-cache memory at long context
acceptance_tests: parameter scale justified by scaling law estimate or ablation
hardware feasibility confirmed for inference serving
revisit_triggers: task scope adds reasoning steps requiring larger context
hardware budget changes

nodes.definition: Choose the model architecture family (decoder-only, encoder-decoder, MoE, sparse) based on specialist task type, generation requirements, and ecosystem maturity of fine-tuning tooling.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new architecture family gains tooling maturity

pros.claim: Decoder-only dominates for generation; MoE offers quality/FLOP efficiency tradeoff
pros.example: Mixtral 8x7B matches 70B on generation at half active params

cons.claim: MoE architectures have higher serving complexity and expert routing latency
cons.example: MoE requires load balancing across GPUs; LoRA support less mature

failure_modes: selecting MoE without serving infrastructure for expert routing
choosing encoder-decoder for open-ended generation tasks
acceptance_tests: fine-tuning toolchain supports chosen architecture
serving infrastructure validated for architecture overhead
revisit_triggers: new MoE family releases with mature tooling
serving infra constraint changes

nodes.definition: Define the fallback chain when a specialist model fails (confidence below threshold, error, timeout): which secondary model receives the request, whether the generalist is the last resort, and how fallback events are logged.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: specialist failure rate exceeds SLA or new fallback model available

pros.claim: Ensures graceful degradation when specialist fails without user-visible errors
pros.example: fallback to generalist during specialist model outage maintains 99.5% uptime

cons.claim: Fallback to expensive generalist can spike costs unexpectedly during incidents
cons.example: traffic spike causes 40% generalist fallback; cost 10x over baseline

failure_modes: no confidence threshold defined so fallback never triggers
fallback chain creates latency cascade beyond SLA
acceptance_tests: fallback triggers tested under simulated specialist failure
fallback cost modeled under worst-case traffic scenario
revisit_triggers: specialist failure rate changes materially
generalist API pricing or availability changes

nodes.definition: Allocate the end-to-end latency budget across orchestration overhead, specialist inference, and fallback paths; validate that selected models can meet P50/P95/P99 targets under expected concurrency.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: traffic concurrency profile changes or hardware tier changes

pros.claim: Exposes model selection infeasibility before GPU spend on training
pros.example: P99 analysis showed 13B model violates 500ms SLA at peak concurrency

cons.claim: Latency benchmarks on dev hardware may not predict prod serving latency under load
cons.example: single-GPU bench showed 200ms; prod with batching showed 850ms P99

failure_modes: benchmarking single requests without concurrency
ignoring orchestration router overhead in budget
acceptance_tests: P99 latency verified under target concurrency on prod-equivalent hardware
orchestration overhead measured and included in budget
revisit_triggers: traffic concurrency grows beyond projected peak
serving hardware changes

nodes.definition: Model tokens-per-second throughput and cost per request under target traffic volume to project monthly GPU spend and identify whether batch inference is viable for the specialist.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: traffic volume or pricing changes materially

pros.claim: Converts abstract model choice into concrete dollar cost enabling budget approval
pros.example: projected 70B model cost exceeds quarterly ML budget; drove 13B selection

cons.claim: Throughput projections depend on batch size and KV-cache behavior that vary in prod
cons.example: batch size assumptions caused 2x cost overrun in first month

failure_modes: projecting cost at single-request throughput ignoring batching gain
ignoring KV-cache eviction cost at long context
acceptance_tests: cost projection validated at 2x expected peak volume
batch vs online split decision documented with rationale
revisit_triggers: actual token volume exceeds projection by >30%
pricing tier changes

nodes.definition: Define the minimum acceptable quality score (task metric, human eval score, business KPI) that any selected specialist model must exceed, establishing the non-negotiable bar before cost/latency tradeoffs are made.
outputs: quality floor spec per task metric

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: business quality requirements revised or user feedback indicates quality regression

pros.claim: Prevents cost-driven model selection from violating user-facing quality commitments
pros.example: quality floor blocked 3B model that saved 60% cost but failed accuracy bar

cons.claim: Poorly calibrated quality floors set too high eliminate cost-effective models without user benefit
cons.example: floor set by engineering intuition rejected model users rated acceptable

failure_modes: setting quality floor from benchmark without business KPI link
treating quality floor as aspirational rather than gating
acceptance_tests: quality floor approved by product owner
quality floor expressed as measurable metric with threshold
revisit_triggers: user quality complaints indicate floor was too low
regulatory requirement raises quality bar

nodes.definition: Configure the evaluation harness to measure specialist task performance consistently across candidate models: dataset, metric implementation, few-shot protocol, and prompt template standardization.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: task prompt template changes or evaluation dataset updated

pros.claim: Standardized harness ensures apples-to-apples model comparison
pros.example: inconsistent prompt templates caused 8% apparent quality difference that was an artifact

cons.claim: Harness configuration itself can introduce bias if template favors certain model families
cons.example: instruction-tuned model benefits more from chat template than base model

failure_modes: different prompt templates per model inflating best model's score
non-reproducible eval due to sampling randomness not seeded
acceptance_tests: eval is reproducible: same result on re-run with fixed seed
prompt template reviewed by domain expert for task alignment
revisit_triggers: model prompt format convention changes
new metric better captures task quality

nodes.definition: Assess whether a domain-pretrained base model (e.g. code, biomedical, legal) provides sufficient task-relevant prior knowledge to warrant selection over a general-purpose base model of similar scale, and quantify the expected quality uplift.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new domain-pretrained model released

pros.claim: Domain pretraining provides vocabulary and knowledge prior that reduces fine-tuning data needed
pros.example: CodeLlama needs 5k code examples vs 50k for general Llama to reach same code quality

cons.claim: Domain-pretrained models may underperform on tasks requiring cross-domain generalization
cons.example: biomedical model poor at legal-medical boundary tasks despite clinical strength

failure_modes: selecting domain model without measuring actual quality uplift
domain model with stale pretraining corpus for fast-evolving domain
acceptance_tests: quality uplift vs general base model quantified on task eval set
pretraining corpus recency verified for domain
revisit_triggers: general base model update closes domain pretraining gap
new domain model family released

nodes.definition: Measure quality degradation and latency/cost benefit from applying post-training quantization (INT8, INT4, GPTQ, AWQ) to shortlisted models to determine whether quantized variants meet the quality floor.
outputs: quality degradation report per quantization level

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new quantization method released or hardware changes

pros.claim: INT4 quantization often reduces memory 4x with <2% quality degradation on most tasks
pros.example: AWQ-quantized 13B fits on single 24GB GPU within quality floor

cons.claim: Quantization quality degradation is task-dependent; reasoning tasks more sensitive
cons.example: INT4 on math reasoning shows 6% degradation exceeding quality floor

failure_modes: benchmarking quantization only on general benchmarks not task-specific eval
ignoring quantization impact on long-context attention quality
acceptance_tests: quantized variant scored on task-specific eval harness
quality delta documented relative to quality floor
revisit_triggers: new quantization method claims improved quality retention
hardware upgrade makes full-precision feasible

nodes.definition: Model the aggregate cost and latency of the full multi-specialist orchestration system accounting for routing overhead, specialist call mix, fallback rates, and compounding latency across the specialist chain.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: specialist mix or traffic routing changes materially

pros.claim: System-level cost view prevents individual optimization that misses compounding effects
pros.example: specialist A optimized alone; chain analysis showed bottleneck at specialist B

cons.claim: Aggregate model requires traffic distribution assumptions that are uncertain at launch
cons.example: initial traffic mix was 60/40; actual was 90/10 causing cost overrun

failure_modes: optimizing specialists in isolation without system-level cost view
ignoring latency compounding in sequential specialist chains
acceptance_tests: aggregate cost modeled under 3 traffic mix scenarios
latency chain validated end-to-end on representative request set
revisit_triggers: actual traffic mix deviates >20% from model assumptions
new specialist added to chain

nodes.definition: Produce an auditable decision record documenting the selected base model per specialist, alternatives considered, rejection rationale, metric evidence, and re-evaluation trigger criteria.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: model replaced or evaluation protocol revised

pros.claim: Auditable record enables post-hoc analysis and regulatory compliance demonstration
pros.example: decision record satisfied model governance audit without additional documentation

cons.claim: Records become stale rapidly in fast-moving model landscape
cons.example: 6-month-old record omits newer models that now dominate Pareto frontier

failure_modes: decision record not updated when model is replaced
alternatives section lists straw-man options without real evaluation
acceptance_tests: decision record includes dated metric evidence for each candidate
re-evaluation triggers are measurable and time-bounded
revisit_triggers: regulatory requirement for model audit trail tightened
selected model deprecated

nodes.definition: Determine whether the specialist's task is narrow enough for a fine-tuned small model to beat a larger generalist, quantifying the task narrowness threshold and required fine-tuning data volume.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: fine-tuning data volume changes or generalist quality jumps

pros.claim: Quantifies when specialization is worth the fine-tuning investment
pros.example: 7B specialist trained on 50k examples beats GPT-4 on medical coding

cons.claim: Narrowness is hard to measure ex ante; often only known post-training
cons.example: task seemed narrow but required broad world knowledge; specialist underperformed

failure_modes: assuming task is narrow without measuring generalist ceiling
insufficient training data for specialist to beat generalist
acceptance_tests: narrowness assessment validated by domain expert
minimum data volume estimated from learning curve extrapolation
revisit_triggers: training data volume changes materially
generalist capability jump closes quality gap

nodes.definition: Define whether and how to use knowledge distillation from a larger teacher model or synthetic data generation to augment training for the specialist base model, respecting teacher model ToS on distillation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: teacher model ToS changes or new distillation technique released

pros.claim: Synthetic data from strong teacher reduces human labeling cost while maintaining quality
pros.example: Orca-style distillation from GPT-4 achieved 80% quality at 5% data cost

cons.claim: Teacher model may prohibit distillation in ToS; violation is high-risk
cons.example: OpenAI ToS prohibits using outputs to train competing models

failure_modes: using distillation-prohibited teacher without legal clearance
synthetic data quality not verified on task eval before training
acceptance_tests: ToS review completed and documented for each teacher model
synthetic data quality verified on held-out eval before training use
revisit_triggers: teacher model ToS updated
synthetic data quality audit shows contamination

nodes.definition: Establish the cadence and triggers for re-evaluating base model selection as new models are released, task requirements evolve, or cost/quality Pareto shifts, to prevent model selection from becoming stale.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: model release cadence changes or quality gap grows

pros.claim: Prevents product from running on obsolete model selection long after better options exist
pros.example: quarterly re-eval caught Llama 3 release that dominated prior selection on cost

cons.claim: Excessive re-evaluation frequency creates engineering churn without proportional benefit
cons.example: monthly re-eval of stable selection wastes 20 engineer-days per cycle

failure_modes: no re-evaluation triggers defined so model selection never reviewed
re-evaluation scope so broad it blocks product releases
acceptance_tests: re-evaluation cadence approved by engineering and product leadership
trigger events are measurable and monitored
revisit_triggers: major model release by dominant provider
task quality regression detected in production

nodes.definition: Detect and mitigate Goodhart's Law effects where optimizing model selection metrics causes selected models to overfit benchmarks rather than improve real-world task performance.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: model selection driven purely by benchmark leaderboard

pros.claim: Prevents selecting models that aced leaderboards but fail on actual user tasks
pros.example: model ranked #1 on public benchmarks ranked #5 on task-specific held-out eval

cons.claim: Goodhart guard requires maintaining held-out eval sets that drift from real distribution over time
cons.example: held-out eval from 2 years ago no longer representative of current user queries

failure_modes: relying solely on public leaderboard for model selection
no held-out task eval separate from benchmark used for selection
acceptance_tests: selection protocol uses at least one eval dataset not in public benchmarks
correlation between benchmark score and task eval score documented
revisit_triggers: benchmark-task correlation drops below threshold
new evidence of widespread benchmark contamination

nodes.definition: Model the operational overhead of serving each shortlisted base model: GPU memory footprint, KV-cache requirements, batching efficiency, and adapter-switching cost for multi-LoRA serving.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: serving infrastructure changes or new multi-LoRA framework released

pros.claim: Prevents model selection that cannot be served on available hardware
pros.example: 13B with 8 LoRA adapters exceeded GPU memory budget; forced 7B selection

cons.claim: Serving overhead models require specific framework knowledge that changes with framework updates
cons.example: vLLM 0.4 changed LoRA memory model; prior estimates invalidated

failure_modes: not modeling KV-cache at max context length
ignoring adapter-switching overhead for multi-tenant serving
acceptance_tests: GPU memory budget verified with KV-cache at P99 context length
multi-LoRA switching overhead measured if more than 3 adapters planned
revisit_triggers: serving framework major version update
adapter count grows beyond initial assumption

edges.resolution_rule: quality floor is non-negotiable gate; cost optimization applies only within floor constraint
use generalist only if it meets quality floor within cost budget; else proceed to fine-tuning
serving overhead gates LoRA choice; if adapter-switching latency breaches SLA, re-evaluate method
contaminated benchmarks disqualified from selection; held-out task eval used as primary signal
ToS prohibiting distillation is a hard block; synthetic data policy cannot override license

conflict_axes.tension_description: reducing model size or using quantization lowers cost but risks falling below quality floor
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: quality floor is non-negotiable; optimize cost within feasible quality-achieving set

conflict_axes.tension_description: frontier API avoids training cost but incurs ongoing per-token cost and latency at scale
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: fine-tune only if quality gap exists AND cost of frontier API exceeds fine-tuned serving at projected volume

conflict_axes.tension_description: LoRA saves memory and enables multi-adapter serving but may leave quality gap on tasks requiring deep weight redistribution
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: default to LoRA; escalate to full FT only when LoRA quality gap exceeds threshold after rank search

conflict_axes.tension_description: public benchmark scores may not correlate with specialist task performance due to contamination and distribution mismatch
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: weight task-specific held-out eval 3x benchmark leaderboard in selection decision

conflict_axes.tension_description: domain-pretrained models improve in-domain performance but may lack cross-domain generalization and have smaller ecosystem
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: use domain model only if measured uplift justifies ecosystem support overhead

conflict_axes.tension_description: larger higher-quality models exceed latency SLA; quantization reduces latency but degrades quality
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: latency SLA and quality floor are both hard constraints; acceptable model set is intersection of both feasible regions

conflict_axes.tension_description: teacher model distillation improves specialist quality cheaply but violates ToS of many frontier models
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: ToS compliance is a hard gate; distillation proceeds only from ToS-permitting teachers

conflict_axes.tension_description: individually optimal specialist models may produce system-level cost and latency violations when combined in chain
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: system-level cost and latency constraints gate individual specialist selection; re-optimize jointly if system budget violated

conflict_axes.tension_description: frequent re-evaluation exploits new models but creates engineering churn; infrequent review risks obsolete selection
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: trigger-based re-evaluation (major release, cost shift, quality regression) over calendar cadence only

conflict_axes.tension_description: aggressive INT4 quantization reduces memory and cost but may breach quality floor on reasoning-heavy tasks
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: quantization level chosen as highest compression that keeps task-specific eval score above quality floor

edge_cases.description: Generalist frontier model quality jumps mid-project, closing gap with planned specialist
edge_cases.trigger: major frontier model release during specialist fine-tuning
edge_cases.recommended_action: halt fine-tuning spend, re-run generalist eval, re-examine ROI of continuing

edge_cases.description: Selected base model weights removed or restricted after selection but before training completes
edge_cases.trigger: model provider pulls weights or changes ToS mid-project
edge_cases.recommended_action: activate secondary shortlist candidate; update decision record; trigger emergency re-selection

edge_cases.description: LoRA quality gap exceeds threshold on production eval but fine-tuning budget exhausted
edge_cases.trigger: LoRA rank search finds no configuration meeting quality floor
edge_cases.recommended_action: request budget for full fine-tuning or accept generalist fallback; escalate to product leadership

edge_cases.description: Benchmark contamination discovered post-selection in model used for final evaluation
edge_cases.trigger: n-gram overlap analysis reveals eval benchmark in model training data
edge_cases.recommended_action: switch to uncontaminated held-out eval; re-score all shortlist candidates; update selection if order changes

edge_cases.description: Multi-specialist cost explodes due to unexpected fallback rate to expensive generalist
edge_cases.trigger: specialist failure rate 3x higher than modeled during incident
edge_cases.recommended_action: implement fallback rate circuit breaker; model fallback cost under incident scenarios in policy

edge_cases.description: Latency SLA tightened by product after model selection complete
edge_cases.trigger: product requirement change reduces P99 SLA by 50%
edge_cases.recommended_action: re-evaluate quantization level; consider smaller model tier; re-run latency budget analysis

edge_cases.description: Domain-pretrained model shows high benchmark score but low task-specific eval score
edge_cases.trigger: domain model pretraining corpus misaligned with specialist task distribution
edge_cases.recommended_action: discard domain model from shortlist; weight task-specific eval; document in Goodhart guard

edge_cases.description: Serving framework update changes LoRA adapter-switching overhead invalidating prior estimates
edge_cases.trigger: major version release of vLLM or TGI changes batching or memory model
edge_cases.recommended_action: re-benchmark serving overhead; update latency budget; confirm LoRA decision still valid

edge_cases.description: Synthetic distillation data quality degrades due to teacher model output drift
edge_cases.trigger: teacher model updated or temperature settings changed mid-data-generation
edge_cases.recommended_action: freeze teacher model version for data generation; re-verify synthetic data on held-out eval

edge_cases.description: Cost/quality Pareto frontier shifts drastically due to pricing change from API provider
edge_cases.trigger: major API provider reduces pricing by >40% making fine-tuning ROI negative
edge_cases.recommended_action: trigger immediate re-evaluation; update cost model; reconsider fine-tuning vs API tradeoff

edge_cases.description: Quality floor set too high eliminates all cost-feasible models
edge_cases.trigger: quality floor negotiated without reference to achievable model quality
edge_cases.recommended_action: present Pareto frontier to stakeholders; negotiate quality floor with evidence of feasibility gap

edge_cases.description: MoE model selected but orchestration infrastructure cannot support expert routing at required concurrency
edge_cases.trigger: serving infrastructure lacks GPU topology for efficient expert routing
edge_cases.recommended_action: fall back to dense architecture from shortlist; document MoE infra requirement for future investment

workflow.input: domain SME interviews, existing pipeline spec, SLA contracts
workflow.output: task profile doc with quality bar, latency/throughput envelope
workflow.gate: task profile approved by domain SME and engineering lead

workflow.input: task profile, business requirements, regulatory constraints
workflow.output: quality floor spec per metric with numeric threshold
workflow.gate: quality floor approved by product owner

workflow.input: candidate model list, deployment architecture, legal team

dominance_rules.condition: quality floor not met by any shortlisted model at any cost level
dominance_rules.dominant_action: halt selection; escalate to product to revise quality floor or increase fine-tuning investment
dominance_rules.rationale: quality floor is a non-negotiable user commitment

dominance_rules.condition: license/ToS prohibits use case for a candidate model
dominance_rules.dominant_action: eliminate model from shortlist regardless of quality or cost superiority
dominance_rules.rationale: legal violation risk is unbounded and irreversible

dominance_rules.condition: benchmark contamination confirmed for primary evaluation metric
dominance_rules.dominant_action: disqualify contaminated benchmark from selection; require uncontaminated task eval
dominance_rules.rationale: contaminated eval produces false confidence in model quality

dominance_rules.condition: generalist frontier model meets quality floor within cost budget
dominance_rules.dominant_action: use generalist API without fine-tuning; defer specialist training unless cost at scale becomes blocking
dominance_rules.rationale: fine-tuning is expensive and risky; skip if generalist suffices

dominance_rules.condition: serving latency SLA violated by selected model at expected concurrency
dominance_rules.dominant_action: descend to smaller parameter tier or apply quantization; do not ship latency-violating model
dominance_rules.rationale: latency SLA is a user-facing commitment

dominance_rules.condition: aggregate multi-specialist system cost exceeds budget under modeled traffic
dominance_rules.dominant_action: re-optimize specialist selection jointly; do not approve individual optimal selections that violate system budget
dominance_rules.rationale: system cost is what the business pays

dominance_rules.condition: distillation teacher model ToS prohibits use of outputs for training
dominance_rules.dominant_action: block distillation from that teacher; use human labels or permissive-license teacher
dominance_rules.rationale: ToS violation creates legal liability and model provider ban risk

dominance_rules.condition: LoRA quality gap exceeds quality floor after full rank search
dominance_rules.dominant_action: escalate to full fine-tuning decision with budget justification; do not ship quality-floor-violating LoRA adapter
dominance_rules.rationale: quality floor governs; PEFT preference is secondary

dominance_rules.condition: re-evaluation trigger event fires (major model release, >20% pricing change, quality regression)
dominance_rules.dominant_action: initiate re-evaluation on current selection; block new specialist additions until re-eval complete if trigger is critical
dominance_rules.rationale: stale model selection compounds cost and quality risk over time

dominance_rules.condition: fallback chain latency cascade exceeds end-to-end SLA under failure scenario
dominance_rules.dominant_action: simplify fallback chain or increase specialist reliability before deployment
dominance_rules.rationale: degraded fallback that violates SLA is worse than controlled error response

anti_rework_rules.rationale: ToS violation discovered after training wastes full fine-tuning GPU budget
quality floor revision post-selection invalidates shortlist and eval harness
harness built on contaminated benchmark must be rebuilt with uncontaminated eval
oversized model discovered post-commitment requires re-selection and re-training

data generated from prohibited teacher must be discarded and regenerated from compliant source
fine-tuning investment discovered to be unnecessary wastes GPU budget and calendar time
adapter-switching overhead discovered post-deployment requires serving re-architecture
selection without triggers becomes permanently stale; revision later requires full re-justification
quantization quality degradation discovered post-deployment forces costly rollback

iteration_protocol.trigger: quality floor not met by any shortlisted model
iteration_protocol.action: re-engage stakeholders to calibrate floor; expand shortlist to higher parameter tiers; consider full fine-tuning
iteration_protocol.convergence_criterion: at least one shortlist model meets quality floor

iteration_protocol.trigger: generalist quality gap exceeds threshold but cost at scale is prohibitive
iteration_protocol.action: initiate fine-tuning decision flow; re-run cost/quality Pareto including fine-tuned specialist option
iteration_protocol.convergence_criterion: selected approach meets both quality floor and budget

iteration_protocol.trigger: LoRA quality gap exceeds floor after rank search
iteration_protocol.action: increase LoRA rank budget; evaluate merged LoRA; escalate to full fine-tuning proposal
iteration_protocol.convergence_criterion: adapter configuration meets quality floor or full FT approved

iteration_protocol.trigger: latency SLA violated by shortlisted models
iteration_protocol.action: descend parameter tier; apply quantization at appropriate level; re-measure latency
iteration_protocol.convergence_criterion: P99 latency within SLA on target concurrency

iteration_protocol.action: identify cost hotspot specialist; re-select that specialist at lower tier; re-model aggregate
iteration_protocol.convergence_criterion: aggregate cost within budget under median traffic scenario

iteration_protocol.action: re-run evaluation harness on new model candidates; compare against current selection Pareto
iteration_protocol.convergence_criterion: decision documented: retain current or replace with evidence

iteration_protocol.trigger: domain-pretrained model uplift less than threshold
iteration_protocol.action: replace domain model with general base model of equivalent scale; re-run shortlisting
iteration_protocol.convergence_criterion: shortlist uses model type justified by measured uplift

iteration_protocol.trigger: Goodhart guard detects benchmark-task correlation below threshold
iteration_protocol.action: discard benchmark from selection; add held-out task eval; re-score candidates
iteration_protocol.convergence_criterion: selection based on uncontaminated task-correlated eval
